tools.name: configuration_view
tools.description: Get the current Kubernetes configuration content as a kubeconfig YAML

minified.description: Return a minified version of the configuration. If set to true, keeps only the current-context and the relevant pieces of the configuration for that context. If set to false, all contexts, clusters, auth-infos, and users are returned in the configuration. (Optional, default true)

tools.name: events_list
tools.description: List Kubernetes events (warnings, errors, state changes) for debugging and troubleshooting in the current cluster from all namespaces

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter events by field values (e.g. 'type=Warning', 'involvedObject.name=my-pod'). Supported fields: involvedObject.kind, involvedObject.name, involvedObject.namespace, involvedObject.uid, involvedObject.apiVersion, involvedObject.resourceVersion, involvedObject.fieldPath, reason, reportingComponent, source, type. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the events from. If not provided, will list events from all namespaces

tools.name: kiali_get_logs
tools.description: Get the logs of a Kubernetes Pod (or workload name that will be resolved to a pod) in a namespace. Output is plain text, matching kubernetes-mcp-server pods_log. The line_count field tells you the total number of log lines returned. Analyze ALL of them, but summarize the results unless the user explicitly asks for the raw output. Do not omit any error or warning lines.

container.description: Optional. Name of the Pod container to get the logs from.

format.description: Output formatting for chat. 'codeblock' wraps logs in ~~~ fences (recommended). 'plain' returns raw text like kubernetes-mcp-server pods_log.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

name.description: Name of the Pod to get the logs from. If it does not exist, it will be treated as a workload name and a running pod will be selected.

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod logs from

previous.description: Optional. Return previous terminated container logs

severity.description: Optional severity filter applied client-side. Accepts 'ERROR', 'WARN' or combinations like 'ERROR,WARN'.

tail.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, defaults to 50). Cannot exceed 200 lines.

workload.description: Optional. Workload name override (used when name lookup fails).

tools.name: kiali_get_mesh_status
tools.description: Retrieves the high-level health, topology, and environment details of the Istio service mesh. Returns multi-cluster control plane status (istiod), data plane namespace health (including ambient mesh status), observability stack health (Prometheus, Grafana...), and component connectivity. Use this tool as the first step to diagnose mesh-wide issues, verify Istio/Kiali versions, or check overall health before drilling into specific workloads.

tools.name: kiali_get_mesh_traffic_graph
tools.description: Returns service-to-service traffic topology, dependencies, and network metrics (throughput, response time, mTLS) for the specified namespaces. Use this to diagnose routing issues, latency, or find upstream/downstream dependencies.

graphType.description: Granularity of the graph. 'app' aggregates by app name, 'versionedApp' separates by versions, 'workload' maps specific pods/deployments. Default: versionedApp.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

namespaces.description: Comma-separated list of namespaces to map

tools.name: kiali_get_metrics
tools.description: Returns a compact JSON summary of Istio metrics (latency quantiles, traffic trends, throughput, payload sizes) for the given resource.

byLabels.description: Comma-separated list of labels to group metrics by (e.g., 'source_workload,destination_service'). Optional

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

quantiles.description: Comma-separated list of quantiles for histogram metrics (e.g., '0.5,0.95,0.99'). Optional

rateInterval.description: Rate interval for metrics (e.g., '1m', '5m'). Optional, defaults to '10m'

reporter.description: Metrics reporter(s). Comma-separated list of: 'source', 'destination', 'waypoint', or the special value 'both' (no reporter filter). Optional, defaults to 'source'. Example: 'source,waypoint'

resourceName.description: Name of the resource to get metrics for

resourceType.description: Type of resource to get metrics

step.description: Step between data points in seconds (e.g., '15'). Optional, defaults to 15 seconds

tools.name: kiali_get_pod_performance
tools.description: Returns a human-readable text summary with current Pod CPU/memory usage (from Prometheus) compared to Kubernetes requests/limits (from the Pod spec). Useful to answer questions like 'Is this workload using too much memory?'

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

podName.description: Kubernetes Pod name. If workloadName is provided, the tool will attempt to resolve a Pod from that workload first.

queryTime.description: Optional end timestamp (RFC3339) for the query. Defaults to now.

timeRange.description: Time window used to compute CPU rate (Prometheus duration like '5m', '10m', '1h', '1d'). Defaults to '10m'.

workloadName.description: Kubernetes Workload name (e.g. Deployment/StatefulSet/etc). Tool will look up the workload and pick one of its Pods. If not found, it will fall back to treating this value as a podName.

tools.name: kiali_get_resource_details
tools.description: Fetches a list of resources OR retrieves detailed data for a specific resource. If 'resourceName' is omitted, it returns a list. If 'resourceName' is provided, it returns details for that specific resource.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

namespaces.description: Comma-separated list of namespaces to query (e.g., 'bookinfo' or 'bookinfo,default'). If not provided, it will query across all accessible namespaces.

resourceName.description: Optional. The specific name of the resource. If left empty, the tool returns a list of all resources of the specified type. If provided, the tool returns deep details for this specific resource.

resourceType.description: The type of resource to query. Use 'app' for Kiali applications (grouped by the Kubernetes 'app' label). Use 'argoapp' for ArgoCD Application CRDs (requires ArgoCD installed and the Kiali service account must have read permissions on applications.argoproj.io).

tools.name: kiali_get_trace_details
tools.description: Fetches a single distributed trace by trace_id and returns its call hierarchy (service tree with duration, status, and nested calls). Use this after list_traces to drill into a specific trace.

traceId.description: Trace ID to fetch and summarize. If provided, namespace/service_name are ignored.

tools.name: kiali_list_mesh_clusters
tools.description: Returns the list of Istio mesh clusters that Kiali can access. Each entry includes its name and whether it is the home cluster (where Kiali is deployed). Call this tool before using meshCluster on other Kiali tools when the target cluster is unknown.

tools.name: kiali_list_traces
tools.description: Lists distributed traces for a service in a namespace. Returns a summary (namespace, service, total_found, avg_duration_ms) and a list of traces with id, duration_ms, spans_count, root_op, slowest_service, has_errors. Use get_trace_details with a trace id to get full hierarchy.

errorOnly.description: If true, only consider traces that contain errors. Default false.

limit.description: Maximum number of traces to return. Default 10.

lookbackSeconds.description: How far back to search. Default 600 (10m).

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

serviceName.description: Service name to search traces for (required). Returns multiple traces up to limit.

tools.name: kiali_manage_istio_config
tools.description: Create, patch, or delete Istio, Gateway API, and Inference API config. Supports Istio resources (networking.istio.io, security.istio.io), Gateway API resources (gateway.networking.k8s.io), and Inference API resources (inference.networking.k8s.io) when installed on the cluster. For list and get (read-only) use manage_istio_config_read.

data.description: JSON or YAML data for the resource. Required for create and patch actions. For create, you can provide partial content (e.g. only spec) and it will be merged onto a valid template with defaults. Arrays (like servers, http, etc.) are REPLACED entirely, so include ALL elements you want.

group.description: API group of the Istio object. Use 'gateway.networking.k8s.io' for Gateway API resources. Use 'inference.networking.k8s.io' for Inference API resources.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

version.description: API version. Use 'v1' for all resource types.

tools.name: kiali_manage_istio_config_read
tools.description: Read Istio, Gateway API, and Inference API config. 'list' groups by namespace→'group/version/kind'→{valid:[...],invalid:[...]} where valid/invalid arrays contain resource names; omit group/kind to retrieve ALL config types in a single call. Supports Istio (networking.istio.io, security.istio.io), Gateway API (gateway.networking.k8s.io), and Inference API (inference.networking.k8s.io) when installed. 'get' returns full YAML. For writes use manage_istio_config.

group.description: API group of the Istio object. Required ONLY for 'get' action. For 'list', OMIT group and kind to retrieve ALL config types in a single call. Use 'gateway.networking.k8s.io' for Gateway API resources. Use 'inference.networking.k8s.io' for Inference API resources.

kind.description: Kind of the Istio object. Required ONLY for 'get' action. For 'list', OMIT to return all kinds at once — do NOT call separately for each kind.

meshCluster.description: Optional Istio mesh cluster name from kiali_list_mesh_clusters (e.g. west). When omitted, Kiali defaults to its home cluster.

namespace.description: Namespace containing the Istio object. For 'list', if not provided, returns objects across all namespaces. For 'get', required.

object.description: Name of the Istio object. Required for 'get' action.

serviceName.description: Filter Istio configurations (VirtualServices, DestinationRules, and their referenced Gateways) that affect a specific service. Only applicable for 'list' action

version.description: API version. Use 'v1' for all resource types. Required for 'get' action.

tools.name: namespaces_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes namespaces in the current cluster

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter namespaces by field values (e.g. 'metadata.name=default', 'status.phase=Active'). Supported fields: metadata.name, status.phase. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

tools.name: nodes_log
tools.description: Get logs from a Kubernetes node (kubelet, kube-proxy, or other system logs). This accesses node logs through the Kubernetes API proxy to the kubelet

name.description: Name of the node to get logs from

query.description: query specifies services(s) or files from which to return logs (required). Example: "kubelet" to fetch kubelet logs, "/<log-file-name>" to fetch a specific log file from the node (e.g., "/var/log/kubelet.log" or "/var/log/kube-proxy.log")

tailLines.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, 0 means all logs)

tools.name: nodes_stats_summary
tools.description: Get detailed resource usage statistics from a Kubernetes node via the kubelet's Summary API. Provides comprehensive metrics including CPU, memory, filesystem, and network usage at the node, pod, and container levels. On systems with cgroup v2 and kernel 4.20+, also includes PSI (Pressure Stall Information) metrics that show resource pressure for CPU, memory, and I/O. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/understand-psi-metrics/ for details on PSI metrics

name.description: Name of the node to get stats from

tools.name: nodes_top
tools.description: List the resource consumption (CPU and memory) as recorded by the Kubernetes Metrics Server for the specified Kubernetes Nodes or all nodes in the cluster

label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=') to filter nodes by label (Optional, only applicable when name is not provided)

name.description: Name of the Node to get the resource consumption from (Optional, all Nodes if not provided)

tools.name: pods_delete
tools.description: Delete a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

name.description: Name of the Pod to delete

namespace.description: Namespace to delete the Pod from

tools.name: pods_exec
tools.description: Execute a command in a Kubernetes Pod (shell access, run commands in container) in the current or provided namespace with the provided name and command

command.description: Command to execute in the Pod container. The first item is the command to be run, and the rest are the arguments to that command. Example: ["ls", "-l", "/tmp"]

container.description: Name of the Pod container where the command will be executed (Optional)

name.description: Name of the Pod where the command will be executed

namespace.description: Namespace of the Pod where the command will be executed

tools.name: pods_get
tools.description: Get a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod from

tools.name: pods_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes pods in the current cluster from all namespaces

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter pods by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'spec.nodeName=node1'). Supported fields: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. Note: CrashLoopBackOff is a container state, not a pod phase, so it cannot be filtered directly. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the pods by label

tools.name: pods_list_in_namespace
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes pods in the specified namespace in the current cluster

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter pods by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'spec.nodeName=node1'). Supported fields: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. Note: CrashLoopBackOff is a container state, not a pod phase, so it cannot be filtered directly. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the pods by label

tools.name: pods_log
tools.description: Get the logs of a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

container.description: Name of the Pod container to get the logs from (Optional)

name.description: Name of the Pod to get the logs from

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod logs from

tail.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, default: 100)

tools.name: pods_run
tools.description: Run a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided container image and optional name

image.description: Container Image to run in the Pod

name.description: Name of the Pod (Optional, random name if not provided)

namespace.description: Namespace to run the Pod in

port.description: TCP/IP port to expose from the Pod container (Optional, no port exposed if not provided)

tools.name: pods_top
tools.description: List the resource consumption (CPU and memory) as recorded by the Kubernetes Metrics Server for the specified Kubernetes Pods in the all namespaces, the provided namespace, or the current namespace

all_namespaces.description: If true, list the resource consumption for all Pods in all namespaces. If false, list the resource consumption for Pods in the provided namespace or the current namespace

label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the pods by label (Optional, only applicable when name is not provided)

name.description: Name of the Pod to get the resource consumption from (Optional, all Pods in the namespace if not provided)

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pods resource consumption from (Optional, current namespace if not provided and all_namespaces is false)

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: List all the OpenShift projects in the current cluster

tools.name: resources_create_or_update
tools.description:
Create or update a Kubernetes resource via Server-Side Apply. The manifest is the complete desired state: any field this tool previously set and the new manifest omits is removed. To edit an existing resource, fetch it with resources_get, modify it, then re-apply the full resource.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

resource.description: Complete YAML or JSON representation of the Kubernetes resource (full desired state, not a partial patch). Include apiVersion, kind, metadata, and the full spec.

tools.name: resources_delete
tools.description:
Delete a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

gracePeriodSeconds.description: Optional duration in seconds before the object should be deleted. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates delete immediately. If this value is nil, the default grace period for the specified type will be used

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to delete the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will delete resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_get
tools.description:
Get a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_list
tools.description:
List Kubernetes resources and objects in the current cluster by providing their apiVersion and kind and optionally the namespace and label selector
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resources (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter resources by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'metadata.name=myresource'). Supported fields vary by resource type. For Pods: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

kind.description: kind of the resources (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the resources by label

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resources from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will list resources from all namespaces

tools.name: resources_scale
tools.description: Get or update the scale of a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, name, and optionally the namespace. If the scale is set in the tool call, the scale will be updated to that value. Always returns the current scale of the resource

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are apps/v1)

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: StatefulSet, Deployment)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to get/update the namespaced resource scale from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get/update resource scale from configured namespace

scale.description: Optional scale to update the resources scale to. If not provided, will return the current scale of the resource, and not update it

Done.

What I found
- The app Deployment specified command: ["/bin/sh","-c"] with args: ["nonexistent_command"], causing the container to exit immediately. Pod logs: “/bin/sh: 1: nonexistent_command: not found”, leading to CrashLoopBackOff.

What I changed
- Recreated the Deployment without the custom command/args so the container uses the image’s default entrypoint.
- Kept labels/selector the same (app=nginx), replicas=1.
- Set image to quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged with imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent and exposed containerPort 8080 (the default for the unprivileged nginx image).

Current status
- Pod is healthy: 1/1 Running in namespace crashloop-test (e.g., app-…-ltwt8).
- No restart/back-off events observed after the fix.

Want me to also create a Service to expose it (ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer) or adjust the port?

Steps.message:
Done.

What I found
- The app Deployment specified command: ["/bin/sh","-c"] with args: ["nonexistent_command"], causing the container to exit immediately. Pod logs: “/bin/sh: 1: nonexistent_command: not found”, leading to CrashLoopBackOff.

What I changed
- Recreated the Deployment without the custom command/args so the container uses the image’s default entrypoint.
- Kept labels/selector the same (app=nginx), replicas=1.
- Set image to quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged with imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent and exposed containerPort 8080 (the default for the unprivileged nginx image).

Current status
- Pod is healthy: 1/1 Running in namespace crashloop-test (e.g., app-…-ltwt8).
- No restart/back-off events observed after the fix.

outputSteps.content:
Done.

What I found
- The app Deployment specified command: ["/bin/sh","-c"] with args: ["nonexistent_command"], causing the container to exit immediately. Pod logs: “/bin/sh: 1: nonexistent_command: not found”, leading to CrashLoopBackOff.

What I changed
- Recreated the Deployment without the custom command/args so the container uses the image’s default entrypoint.
- Kept labels/selector the same (app=nginx), replicas=1.
- Set image to quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged with imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent and exposed containerPort 8080 (the default for the unprivileged nginx image).

Current status
- Pod is healthy: 1/1 Running in namespace crashloop-test (e.g., app-…-ltwt8).
- No restart/back-off events observed after the fix.

Want me to also create a Service to expose it (ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer) or adjust the port?

results.taskOutput:
Fixed.

What happened
- Root cause: The pod requested a PVC (homepage-pvc) with storageClass "sc", but that StorageClass doesn’t exist. Scheduler blocked the pod with “pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims.”

What I changed
- Deleted the pending PVC (it had no backing volume/data yet).
- Recreated it using an available StorageClass: standard (minikube-hostpath).

Current status
- PVC homepage-pvc: Bound to volume pvc-dc6c6705-23c9-4b9a-a6fc-725b85692c09, 1Gi.
- Pod homepage-pod: Running and Ready on node mcp-eval-cluster; container nginx is up.

Notes
- storageClassName on a PVC is immutable; recreating the PVC was required.
- If you prefer a different StorageClass (e.g., csi-hostpath-sc), tell me and I can switch it.

outputSteps.content:
Fixed.

What happened
- Root cause: The pod requested a PVC (homepage-pvc) with storageClass "sc", but that StorageClass doesn’t exist. Scheduler blocked the pod with “pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims.”

What I changed
- Deleted the pending PVC (it had no backing volume/data yet).
- Recreated it using an available StorageClass: standard (minikube-hostpath).

Current status
- PVC homepage-pvc: Bound to volume pvc-dc6c6705-23c9-4b9a-a6fc-725b85692c09, 1Gi.
- Pod homepage-pod: Running and Ready on node mcp-eval-cluster; container nginx is up.

Notes
- storageClassName on a PVC is immutable; recreating the PVC was required.
- If you prefer a different StorageClass (e.g., csi-hostpath-sc), tell me and I can switch it.

results.taskOutput:
I found and fixed two issues in orders/webapp:

Root cause
- The nginx-unprivileged image listens on 8080 (not 80), but the Deployment health probes were calling port 80 on non-existent paths (/get_status, /is_ready). This caused liveness/readiness failures.
- The Service targeted port 80, so even if the pod was healthy on 8080, the service wouldn’t reach it.

What I changed
- Deployment: updated probes to GET / on port 8080 and exposed container port 8080.
- Service: updated targetPort to 8080 (port 80 -> targetPort 8080), name “http”.

Current status
- Pod is healthy: orders/webapp-5fb688dc88-jdcs4 is 1/1 Running.
- Service webapp now points to the correct targetPort (8080).

How to verify
- Port-forward: kubectl -n orders port-forward svc/webapp 8080:80 and open http://localhost:8080/
- In-cluster curl: kubectl run -it --rm curl --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -- curl http://webapp.orders.svc.cluster.local/

If you need this exposed externally (Ingress/Gateway), tell me how you prefer to expose it and I’ll configure that as well.

Steps.message:
namespace/orders created
deployment.apps/webapp created
service/webapp created
Waiting for pod to start and begin failing health checks...
deployment.apps/webapp condition met
Setup successful: Deployment is no longer available.

I found and fixed two issues in orders/webapp:

Root cause
- The nginx-unprivileged image listens on 8080 (not 80), but the Deployment health probes were calling port 80 on non-existent paths (/get_status, /is_ready). This caused liveness/readiness failures.
- The Service targeted port 80, so even if the pod was healthy on 8080, the service wouldn’t reach it.

What I changed
- Deployment: updated probes to GET / on port 8080 and exposed container port 8080.
- Service: updated targetPort to 8080 (port 80 -> targetPort 8080), name “http”.

Current status
- Pod is healthy: orders/webapp-5fb688dc88-jdcs4 is 1/1 Running.
- Service webapp now points to the correct targetPort (8080).

How to verify
- Port-forward: kubectl -n orders port-forward svc/webapp 8080:80 and open http://localhost:8080/
- In-cluster curl: kubectl run -it --rm curl --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -- curl http://webapp.orders.svc.cluster.local/

If you need this exposed externally (Ingress/Gateway), tell me how you prefer to expose it and I’ll configure that as well.

outputSteps.content:
I found and fixed two issues in orders/webapp:

Root cause
- The nginx-unprivileged image listens on 8080 (not 80), but the Deployment health probes were calling port 80 on non-existent paths (/get_status, /is_ready). This caused liveness/readiness failures.
- The Service targeted port 80, so even if the pod was healthy on 8080, the service wouldn’t reach it.

What I changed
- Deployment: updated probes to GET / on port 8080 and exposed container port 8080.
- Service: updated targetPort to 8080 (port 80 -> targetPort 8080), name “http”.

Current status
- Pod is healthy: orders/webapp-5fb688dc88-jdcs4 is 1/1 Running.
- Service webapp now points to the correct targetPort (8080).

How to verify
- Port-forward: kubectl -n orders port-forward svc/webapp 8080:80 and open http://localhost:8080/
- In-cluster curl: kubectl run -it --rm curl --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -- curl http://webapp.orders.svc.cluster.local/

If you need this exposed externally (Ingress/Gateway), tell me how you prefer to expose it and I’ll configure that as well.

Root cause
- The Role bound to your service account only allowed listing apps/deployments, not core/v1 pods. So the pod-reader SA had no permission to list pods in simple-rbac-setup.

What I changed
- Updated Role simple-rbac-setup/pod-reader-role to include permission to list core/v1 pods (kept the existing deployments rule):
  - apiGroups: [""], resources: ["pods"], verbs: ["list"]
- Your existing RoleBinding pod-reader-binding already points to this Role and to ServiceAccount simple-rbac-setup/pod-reader, so no change was needed there.

How to verify
- kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:simple-rbac-setup:pod-reader -n simple-rbac-setup list pods
  Expected: yes
- kubectl get pods -n simple-rbac-setup --as=system:serviceaccount:simple-rbac-setup:pod-reader

Optional
- If you also want to watch or get individual pods, I can add verbs ["get","watch"] as well.

outputSteps.content:
Root cause
- The Role bound to your service account only allowed listing apps/deployments, not core/v1 pods. So the pod-reader SA had no permission to list pods in simple-rbac-setup.

What I changed
- Updated Role simple-rbac-setup/pod-reader-role to include permission to list core/v1 pods (kept the existing deployments rule):
  - apiGroups: [""], resources: ["pods"], verbs: ["list"]
- Your existing RoleBinding pod-reader-binding already points to this Role and to ServiceAccount simple-rbac-setup/pod-reader, so no change was needed there.

How to verify
- kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:simple-rbac-setup:pod-reader -n simple-rbac-setup list pods
  Expected: yes
- kubectl get pods -n simple-rbac-setup --as=system:serviceaccount:simple-rbac-setup:pod-reader

Optional
- If you also want to watch or get individual pods, I can add verbs ["get","watch"] as well.

Steps.message: Verification successful: RBAC role correctly reconfigured.

results.taskOutput:
Root cause
- The Service selector didn’t match the Pod labels, so it had no endpoints. Service selector was app=web while the nginx Pod is labeled app=nginx. With no endpoints, the Service could not route traffic.

What I changed (fix applied)
- Updated Service web/nginx to select app=nginx.
- Result: the Endpoints now include the nginx Pod.
  - Endpoints: 10.244.0.40:80
  - Service: ClusterIP 10.100.187.124:80
  - Pod: web/nginx-6d94b64d45-549xn (1/1 Running)
  - No warning Events in namespace web

What “accessible” means and next steps
- Inside the cluster: It should now be reachable at:
  - DNS: http://nginx.web.svc.cluster.local
  - ClusterIP: http://10.100.187.124
- From outside the cluster: The Service is type ClusterIP (internal only). There’s no Ingress defined. Pick one of these and I can set it up:
  1) Quick test (no config): kubectl -n web port-forward svc/nginx 8080:80 then browse http://localhost:8080
  2) LoadBalancer Service (if your cluster/cloud supports it): I can change the Service to type: LoadBalancer to get an external IP.
  3) NodePort Service: expose a high port on each node.
  4) Ingress: if you have an Ingress controller, I can create an Ingress (e.g., host nginx.example.com -> svc/nginx:80).

Tell me which exposure you prefer (LoadBalancer, NodePort, or Ingress + desired host), and I’ll apply it.

Steps.message:
namespace/web created
deployment.apps/nginx created
service/nginx created

Root cause
- The Service selector didn’t match the Pod labels, so it had no endpoints. Service selector was app=web while the nginx Pod is labeled app=nginx. With no endpoints, the Service could not route traffic.

What I changed (fix applied)
- Updated Service web/nginx to select app=nginx.
- Result: the Endpoints now include the nginx Pod.
  - Endpoints: 10.244.0.40:80
  - Service: ClusterIP 10.100.187.124:80
  - Pod: web/nginx-6d94b64d45-549xn (1/1 Running)
  - No warning Events in namespace web

What “accessible” means and next steps
- Inside the cluster: It should now be reachable at:
  - DNS: http://nginx.web.svc.cluster.local
  - ClusterIP: http://10.100.187.124
- From outside the cluster: The Service is type ClusterIP (internal only). There’s no Ingress defined. Pick one of these and I can set it up:
  1) Quick test (no config): kubectl -n web port-forward svc/nginx 8080:80 then browse http://localhost:8080
  2) LoadBalancer Service (if your cluster/cloud supports it): I can change the Service to type: LoadBalancer to get an external IP.
  3) NodePort Service: expose a high port on each node.
  4) Ingress: if you have an Ingress controller, I can create an Ingress (e.g., host nginx.example.com -> svc/nginx:80).

Tell me which exposure you prefer (LoadBalancer, NodePort, or Ingress + desired host), and I’ll apply it.

outputSteps.content:
Root cause
- The Service selector didn’t match the Pod labels, so it had no endpoints. Service selector was app=web while the nginx Pod is labeled app=nginx. With no endpoints, the Service could not route traffic.

What I changed (fix applied)
- Updated Service web/nginx to select app=nginx.
- Result: the Endpoints now include the nginx Pod.
  - Endpoints: 10.244.0.40:80
  - Service: ClusterIP 10.100.187.124:80
  - Pod: web/nginx-6d94b64d45-549xn (1/1 Running)
  - No warning Events in namespace web

What “accessible” means and next steps
- Inside the cluster: It should now be reachable at:
  - DNS: http://nginx.web.svc.cluster.local
  - ClusterIP: http://10.100.187.124
- From outside the cluster: The Service is type ClusterIP (internal only). There’s no Ingress defined. Pick one of these and I can set it up:
  1) Quick test (no config): kubectl -n web port-forward svc/nginx 8080:80 then browse http://localhost:8080
  2) LoadBalancer Service (if your cluster/cloud supports it): I can change the Service to type: LoadBalancer to get an external IP.
  3) NodePort Service: expose a high port on each node.
  4) Ingress: if you have an Ingress controller, I can create an Ingress (e.g., host nginx.example.com -> svc/nginx:80).

Tell me which exposure you prefer (LoadBalancer, NodePort, or Ingress + desired host), and I’ll apply it.

results.taskOutput:
Diagnosis
- Root cause: The Deployment had a nodeSelector environment=production-gpu, but no node in the cluster has that label. Scheduler events show FailedScheduling: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.
- Impact: No pods were running behind web-app-service, so the service had no endpoints and calls to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local returned connection refused.

What I changed
- Updated the web-app-deployment to remove the nodeSelector so it can schedule on available nodes.

Verification
- Pods: 2/2 pods are Running
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-7rh68 1/1 Running
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-f4wvv 1/1 Running
- Deployment: Available=True, readyReplicas=2, updatedReplicas=2.
- Service endpoints for web-app-service now include:
  - 10.244.0.44:80
  - 10.244.0.45:80

Why this fixes the issue
- With pods now running and selected by the Service (selector app=web-app), the service endpoints are populated. Traffic to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local:80 should succeed instead of being refused.

Follow-ups and recommendations
- If the intent was to run on GPU nodes, either:
  - Label the target nodes with environment=production-gpu, or
  - Adjust the Deployment to match the correct label(s) actually present on your GPU nodes.
- Consider adding readinessProbes to avoid any brief 503/connection errors during startup or future rollouts.
- Consider pinning a specific image tag instead of latest for reproducible deployments (e.g., quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:1.29).

namespace/webshop-frontend created
service/web-app-service created
deployment.apps/web-app-deployment created
Waiting for resources to be created...
deployment.apps/web-app-deployment condition met
Warning: v1 Endpoints is deprecated in v1.33+; use discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlice
Setup successful: Service has no endpoints as expected

Diagnosis
- Root cause: The Deployment had a nodeSelector environment=production-gpu, but no node in the cluster has that label. Scheduler events show FailedScheduling: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.
- Impact: No pods were running behind web-app-service, so the service had no endpoints and calls to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local returned connection refused.

What I changed
- Updated the web-app-deployment to remove the nodeSelector so it can schedule on available nodes.

Verification
- Pods: 2/2 pods are Running
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-7rh68 1/1 Running
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-f4wvv 1/1 Running
- Deployment: Available=True, readyReplicas=2, updatedReplicas=2.
- Service endpoints for web-app-service now include:
  - 10.244.0.44:80
  - 10.244.0.45:80

Why this fixes the issue
- With pods now running and selected by the Service (selector app=web-app), the service endpoints are populated. Traffic to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local:80 should succeed instead of being refused.

Follow-ups and recommendations
- If the intent was to run on GPU nodes, either:
  - Label the target nodes with environment=production-gpu, or
  - Adjust the Deployment to match the correct label(s) actually present on your GPU nodes.
- Consider adding readinessProbes to avoid any brief 503/connection errors during startup or future rollouts.
- Consider pinning a specific image tag instead of latest for reproducible deployments (e.g., quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:1.29).

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app-deployment
  namespace: webshop-frontend
  labels:
    app: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-app
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-app
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {}
      containers:
        - name: web-app-container
          image: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
              protocol: TCP
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      schedulerName: default-scheduler
      securityContext: {}
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

kind: Deployment

  name: web-app-deployment
  namespace: webshop-frontend
  labels:

  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-app
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-app
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {}
      containers:
        - name: web-app-container
          image: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80

      restartPolicy: Always
      schedulerName: default-scheduler
      securityContext: {}
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

Diagnosis
- Root cause: The Deployment had a nodeSelector environment=production-gpu, but no node in the cluster has that label. Scheduler events show FailedScheduling: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.
- Impact: No pods were running behind web-app-service, so the service had no endpoints and calls to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local returned connection refused.

What I changed
- Updated the web-app-deployment to remove the nodeSelector so it can schedule on available nodes.

Verification
- Pods: 2/2 pods are Running
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-7rh68 1/1 Running
  - web-app-deployment-6748d646cb-f4wvv 1/1 Running
- Deployment: Available=True, readyReplicas=2, updatedReplicas=2.
- Service endpoints for web-app-service now include:
  - 10.244.0.44:80
  - 10.244.0.45:80

Why this fixes the issue
- With pods now running and selected by the Service (selector app=web-app), the service endpoints are populated. Traffic to web-app-service.webshop-frontend.svc.cluster.local:80 should succeed instead of being refused.

Follow-ups and recommendations
- If the intent was to run on GPU nodes, either:
  - Label the target nodes with environment=production-gpu, or
  - Adjust the Deployment to match the correct label(s) actually present on your GPU nodes.
- Consider adding readinessProbes to avoid any brief 503/connection errors during startup or future rollouts.
- Consider pinning a specific image tag instead of latest for reproducible deployments (e.g., quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:1.29).

- Hit the web server to generate logs (from within cluster): kubectl exec -n multi-container-logging pod/communication-pod -c logger -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/
- Re-check logger logs to see access entries.

Steps.message:
Done. I created the namespace and ran the pod as requested.

What I set up:
- Namespace: multi-container-logging
- Pod: communication-pod
- Volumes: logs-volume (emptyDir)
- Containers (both under spec.containers):
  - web-server: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:latest
    - Ports: 8080
    - Mounts: logs-volume at /var/log/nginx
    - Readiness probe: HTTP GET / on port 8080 (pod is Ready when the web server serves traffic)
  - logger: quay.io/prometheus/busybox:latest
    - Command: sh -c "tail -f /var/log/nginx/access.log"
    - Mounts: logs-volume at /var/log/nginx

Current status:
- Pod phase: Running
- Pod conditions: Ready = True, ContainersReady = True
- Both containers are running and Ready.

How to verify quickly:
- Check logger output: kubectl logs -n multi-container-logging pod/communication-pod -c logger --tail=50
- Hit the web server to generate logs (from within cluster): kubectl exec -n multi-container-logging pod/communication-pod -c logger -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/
- Re-check logger logs to see access entries.

results.taskOutput:
All set. I’ve created the namespaces, RBAC, service accounts, resource quotas, and network policies to meet your requirements and enforce least privilege.

What I configured
1) Namespaces
- Created: dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, dev-shared, staging, prod
- Labeled with env and tenant (where applicable) to aid policy/ops

2) RBAC and Service Accounts
- ServiceAccounts: alice-sa (dev-alice), bob-sa (dev-bob), charlie-sa (dev-charlie)
- Per-developer namespace access:
  - Each developer user (alice/bob/charlie) and their SA are bound to ClusterRole edit in their own namespace (create/update most resources but no RBAC changes, aligning with least privilege)
- Shared namespace access:
  - dev-shared grants read-only (ClusterRole view) to users alice, bob, charlie and the three SAs
- Staging/prod:
  - No RoleBindings were created for developers. Only cluster-admins (e.g., members of system:masters) will have access. If you have a custom admin group, we can explicitly bind it.

3) Resource Quotas
- dev-alice/dev-bob/dev-charlie:
  - requests.cpu=2, limits.cpu=2, requests.memory=4Gi, limits.memory=4Gi, pods=10, services=5
- dev-shared:
  - requests.cpu=4, limits.cpu=4, requests.memory=8Gi, limits.memory=8Gi, pods=20, services=10
- staging/prod:
  - requests.cpu=8, limits.cpu=8, requests.memory=16Gi, limits.memory=16Gi, pods=50, services=20

4) Network Policies (isolation and least privilege)
- Default deny (ingress and egress) in dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, dev-shared, staging, prod
- DNS egress allowed to kube-system: UDP/TCP 53 in all six namespaces
- Developer namespaces:
  - Ingress: only from same namespace
  - Egress: to same-namespace pods, and to dev-shared only
- dev-shared:
  - Ingress allowed from dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, and dev-shared (so dev pods can consume shared services)
  - Egress limited to same-namespace pods (+DNS)
- staging and prod:
  - Completely isolated from dev namespaces
  - Ingress/egress only within their own namespace (+DNS)

Notes and optional adjustments
- “Full access to namespace”: I bound users/SAs to ClusterRole edit (no RBAC changes). If you want developers to also manage RBAC within their namespace, switch to ClusterRole admin in their namespace; say the word and I’ll update.
- Access to Kubernetes API from Pods: Default-deny egress blocks pod-initiated calls to kubernetes.default.svc (TCP 443). If your workloads need that, I can add a precise allow-egress-to-API rule.
- System namespaces: No default-deny policies were applied to system namespaces (e.g., kube-system), as requested.

How to use the developer service accounts (Kubernetes v1.24+)
- kubectl -n dev-alice create token alice-sa
- kubectl -n dev-bob create token bob-sa
- kubectl -n dev-charlie create token charlie-sa

Quick verification
- RBAC:
  - kubectl auth can-i create deploy -n dev-alice --as alice           (yes)
  - kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-shared --as alice               (yes)
  - kubectl auth can-i get pods -n staging --as alice                  (no)
- Network isolation:
  - From a pod in dev-alice, curl a service in dev-bob (should fail)
  - From a pod in dev-alice, curl a service in dev-shared (should succeed)
  - From staging/prod, cross-namespace traffic (should fail)

If you want me to:
- Switch developer access from edit to admin in their namespaces,
- Add specific egress to kubernetes.default.svc:443,
- Add LimitRanges to enforce per-pod defaults,
just let me know and I’ll apply those updates.

Steps.message:
Setting up cluster state for dev environment eval...
Setup completed successfully

All set. I’ve created the namespaces, RBAC, service accounts, resource quotas, and network policies to meet your requirements and enforce least privilege.

What I configured
1) Namespaces
- Created: dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, dev-shared, staging, prod
- Labeled with env and tenant (where applicable) to aid policy/ops

2) RBAC and Service Accounts
- ServiceAccounts: alice-sa (dev-alice), bob-sa (dev-bob), charlie-sa (dev-charlie)
- Per-developer namespace access:
  - Each developer user (alice/bob/charlie) and their SA are bound to ClusterRole edit in their own namespace (create/update most resources but no RBAC changes, aligning with least privilege)
- Shared namespace access:
  - dev-shared grants read-only (ClusterRole view) to users alice, bob, charlie and the three SAs
- Staging/prod:
  - No RoleBindings were created for developers. Only cluster-admins (e.g., members of system:masters) will have access. If you have a custom admin group, we can explicitly bind it.

3) Resource Quotas
- dev-alice/dev-bob/dev-charlie:
  - requests.cpu=2, limits.cpu=2, requests.memory=4Gi, limits.memory=4Gi, pods=10, services=5
- dev-shared:
  - requests.cpu=4, limits.cpu=4, requests.memory=8Gi, limits.memory=8Gi, pods=20, services=10
- staging/prod:
  - requests.cpu=8, limits.cpu=8, requests.memory=16Gi, limits.memory=16Gi, pods=50, services=20

4) Network Policies (isolation and least privilege)
- Default deny (ingress and egress) in dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, dev-shared, staging, prod
- DNS egress allowed to kube-system: UDP/TCP 53 in all six namespaces
- Developer namespaces:
  - Ingress: only from same namespace
  - Egress: to same-namespace pods, and to dev-shared only
- dev-shared:
  - Ingress allowed from dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, and dev-shared (so dev pods can consume shared services)
  - Egress limited to same-namespace pods (+DNS)
- staging and prod:
  - Completely isolated from dev namespaces
  - Ingress/egress only within their own namespace (+DNS)

Notes and optional adjustments
- “Full access to namespace”: I bound users/SAs to ClusterRole edit (no RBAC changes). If you want developers to also manage RBAC within their namespace, switch to ClusterRole admin in their namespace; say the word and I’ll update.
- Access to Kubernetes API from Pods: Default-deny egress blocks pod-initiated calls to kubernetes.default.svc (TCP 443). If your workloads need that, I can add a precise allow-egress-to-API rule.
- System namespaces: No default-deny policies were applied to system namespaces (e.g., kube-system), as requested.

How to use the developer service accounts (Kubernetes v1.24+)
- kubectl -n dev-alice create token alice-sa
- kubectl -n dev-bob create token bob-sa
- kubectl -n dev-charlie create token charlie-sa

Quick verification
- RBAC:
  - kubectl auth can-i create deploy -n dev-alice --as alice           (yes)
  - kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-shared --as alice               (yes)
  - kubectl auth can-i get pods -n staging --as alice                  (no)
- Network isolation:
  - From a pod in dev-alice, curl a service in dev-bob (should fail)
  - From a pod in dev-alice, curl a service in dev-shared (should succeed)
  - From staging/prod, cross-namespace traffic (should fail)

If you want me to:
- Switch developer access from edit to admin in their namespaces,
- Add specific egress to kubernetes.default.svc:443,
- Add LimitRanges to enforce per-pod defaults,
just let me know and I’ll apply those updates.

outputSteps.content:
All set. I’ve created the namespaces, RBAC, service accounts, resource quotas, and network policies to meet your requirements and enforce least privilege.

What I configured
1) Namespaces
- Created: dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, dev-shared, staging, prod
- Labeled with env and tenant (where applicable) to aid policy/ops

2) RBAC and Service Accounts
- ServiceAccounts: alice-sa (dev-alice), bob-sa (dev-bob), charlie-sa (dev-charlie)
- Per-developer namespace access:
  - Each developer user (alice/bob/charlie) and their SA are bound to ClusterRole edit in their own namespace (create/update most resources but no RBAC changes, aligning with least privilege)
- Shared namespace access:
  - dev-shared grants read-only (ClusterRole view) to users alice, bob, charlie and the three SAs
- Staging/prod:
  - No RoleBindings were created for developers. Only cluster-admins (e.g., members of system:masters) will have access. If you have a custom admin group, we can explicitly bind it.

3) Resource Quotas
- dev-alice/dev-bob/dev-charlie:
  - requests.cpu=2, limits.cpu=2, requests.memory=4Gi, limits.memory=4Gi, pods=10, services=5
- dev-shared:
  - requests.cpu=4, limits.cpu=4, requests.memory=8Gi, limits.memory=8Gi, pods=20, services=10
- staging/prod:
  - requests.cpu=8, limits.cpu=8, requests.memory=16Gi, limits.memory=16Gi, pods=50, services=20

4) Network Policies (isolation and least privilege)
- Default deny (ingress and egress) in dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, dev-shared, staging, prod
- DNS egress allowed to kube-system: UDP/TCP 53 in all six namespaces
- Developer namespaces:
  - Ingress: only from same namespace
  - Egress: to same-namespace pods, and to dev-shared only
- dev-shared:
  - Ingress allowed from dev-alice, dev-bob, dev-charlie, and dev-shared (so dev pods can consume shared services)
  - Egress limited to same-namespace pods (+DNS)
- staging and prod:
  - Completely isolated from dev namespaces
  - Ingress/egress only within their own namespace (+DNS)

Notes and optional adjustments
- “Full access to namespace”: I bound users/SAs to ClusterRole edit (no RBAC changes). If you want developers to also manage RBAC within their namespace, switch to ClusterRole admin in their namespace; say the word and I’ll update.
- Access to Kubernetes API from Pods: Default-deny egress blocks pod-initiated calls to kubernetes.default.svc (TCP 443). If your workloads need that, I can add a precise allow-egress-to-API rule.
- System namespaces: No default-deny policies were applied to system namespaces (e.g., kube-system), as requested.

How to use the developer service accounts (Kubernetes v1.24+)
- kubectl -n dev-alice create token alice-sa
- kubectl -n dev-bob create token bob-sa
- kubectl -n dev-charlie create token charlie-sa

Quick verification
- RBAC:
  - kubectl auth can-i create deploy -n dev-alice --as alice           (yes)
  - kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-shared --as alice               (yes)
  - kubectl auth can-i get pods -n staging --as alice                  (no)
- Network isolation:
  - From a pod in dev-alice, curl a service in dev-bob (should fail)
  - From a pod in dev-alice, curl a service in dev-shared (should succeed)
  - From staging/prod, cross-namespace traffic (should fail)

If you want me to:
- Switch developer access from edit to admin in their namespaces,
- Add specific egress to kubernetes.default.svc:443,
- Add LimitRanges to enforce per-pod defaults,
just let me know and I’ll apply those updates.

spec.description: Spec defines the desired state of the InferencePool.

appProtocol.description:
AppProtocol describes the application protocol for all the target ports.

If unspecified, the protocol defaults to HTTP/1.1.

Supported values include:
* "http": HTTP/1.1. This is the default.
* "kubernetes.io/h2c": HTTP/2 over cleartext.

endpointPickerRef.description:
EndpointPickerRef is a reference to the Endpoint Picker extension and its
associated configuration.

failureMode.description:
FailureMode configures how the parent handles the case when the Endpoint Picker extension
is non-responsive. When unspecified, defaults to "FailClose".

group.description:
Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the default value
is "", representing the Core API group.

kind.description:
Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind of the referent.

Required if the referent is ambiguous, e.g. service with multiple ports.

Defaults to "Service" when not specified.

ExternalName services can refer to CNAME DNS records that may live
outside of the cluster and as such are difficult to reason about in
terms of conformance. They also may not be safe to forward to (see
CVE-2021-25740 for more information). Implementations MUST NOT
support ExternalName Services.

name.description: Name is the name of the referent API object.

port.description:
Port is the port of the Endpoint Picker extension service.

Port is required when the referent is a Kubernetes Service. In this
case, the port number is the service port number, not the target port.
For other resources, destination port might be derived from the referent
resource or this field.

number.description:
Number defines the port number to access the selected model server Pods.
The number must be in the range 1 to 65535.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: port is required when kind is 'Service' or unspecified (defaults to 'Service')

selector.description:
Selector determines which Pods are members of this inference pool.
It matches Pods by their labels only within the same namespace; cross-namespace
selection is not supported.

The structure of this LabelSelector is intentionally simple to be compatible
with Kubernetes Service selectors, as some implementations may translate
this configuration into a Service resource.

additionalProperties.description:
LabelValue is the value of a label. This is used for validation
of maps. This matches the Kubernetes label validation rules:
* must be 63 characters or less (can be empty),
* unless empty, must begin and end with an alphanumeric character ([a-z0-9A-Z]),
* could contain dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.

Valid values include:

* MyValue
* my.name
* 123-my-value

matchLabels.description:
MatchLabels contains a set of required {key,value} pairs.
An object must match every label in this map to be selected.
The matching logic is an AND operation on all entries.

targetPorts.description:
TargetPorts defines a list of ports that are exposed by this InferencePool.
Every port will be treated as a distinctive endpoint by EPP,
addressable as a 'podIP:portNumber' combination.

items.description: Port defines the network port that will be exposed by this InferencePool.

number.description:
Number defines the port number to access the selected model server Pods.
The number must be in the range 1 to 65535.

status.description: Status defines the observed state of the InferencePool.

parents.description:
Parents is a list of parent resources, typically Gateways, that are associated with
the InferencePool, and the status of the InferencePool with respect to each parent.

A controller that manages the InferencePool, must add an entry for each parent it manages
and remove the parent entry when the controller no longer considers the InferencePool to
be associated with that parent.

A maximum of 32 parents will be represented in this list. When the list is empty,
it indicates that the InferencePool is not associated with any parents.

items.description: ParentStatus defines the observed state of InferencePool from a Parent, i.e. Gateway.

conditions.description:
Conditions is a list of status conditions that provide information about the observed
state of the InferencePool. This field is required to be set by the controller that
manages the InferencePool.

Supported condition types are:

* "Accepted"
* "ResolvedRefs"

items.description: Condition contains details for one aspect of the current state of this API Resource.

lastTransitionTime.description:
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description:
message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description:
reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
The value should be a CamelCase string.
This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.

controllerName.description:
ControllerName is a domain/path string that indicates the name of the controller that
wrote this status. This corresponds with the GatewayClass controllerName field when the
parentRef references a Gateway kind.

Example: "example.net/gateway-controller".

The format of this field is DOMAIN "/" PATH, where DOMAIN and PATH are valid Kubernetes names:

 https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

Controllers MAY populate this field when writing status. When populating this field, controllers
should ensure that entries to status populated with their ControllerName are cleaned up when they
are no longer necessary.

parentRef.description:
ParentRef is used to identify the parent resource that this status
is associated with. It is used to match the InferencePool with the parent
resource, such as a Gateway.

group.description:
Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed
to be in the "gateway.networking.k8s.io" API group.

kind.description:
Kind is the kind of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed
to be a "Gateway" kind.

name.description: Name is the name of the referent API object.

namespace.description:
Namespace is the namespace of the referenced object. When unspecified, the local
namespace is inferred.

Note that when a namespace different than the local namespace is specified,
a ReferenceGrant object is required in the referent namespace to allow that
namespace's owner to accept the reference. See the ReferenceGrant
documentation for details: https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/api-types/referencegrant/

        properties:
          apiVersion:

              Cannot be updated.

              More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
            type: string
          metadata:
            type: object
          spec:
            description: Spec defines the desired state of the InferencePool.
            properties:
              appProtocol:
                default: http
                description: |-
                  AppProtocol describes the application protocol for all the target ports.

                  If unspecified, the protocol defaults to HTTP/1.1.

                  Supported values include:
                  * "http": HTTP/1.1. This is the default.
                  * "kubernetes.io/h2c": HTTP/2 over cleartext.
                enum:
                - http
                - kubernetes.io/h2c
                type: string
              endpointPickerRef:
                description: |-
                  EndpointPickerRef is a reference to the Endpoint Picker extension and its
                  associated configuration.
                properties:
                  failureMode:
                    default: FailClose
                    description: |-
                      FailureMode configures how the parent handles the case when the Endpoint Picker extension
                      is non-responsive. When unspecified, defaults to "FailClose".
                    enum:
                    - FailOpen
                    - FailClose
                    type: string
                  group:
                    default: ""
                    description: |-
                      Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the default value
                      is "", representing the Core API group.
                    maxLength: 253
                    minLength: 0
                    pattern: ^$|^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$
                    type: string
                  kind:
                    default: Service
                    description: |-
                      Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind of the referent.

                      Required if the referent is ambiguous, e.g. service with multiple ports.

                      Defaults to "Service" when not specified.

                      ExternalName services can refer to CNAME DNS records that may live
                      outside of the cluster and as such are difficult to reason about in
                      terms of conformance. They also may not be safe to forward to (see
                      CVE-2021-25740 for more information). Implementations MUST NOT
                      support ExternalName Services.
                    maxLength: 63
                    minLength: 1
                    pattern: ^[a-zA-Z]([-a-zA-Z0-9]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$
                    type: string
                  name:
                    description: Name is the name of the referent API object.
                    maxLength: 253
                    minLength: 1
                    type: string
                  port:
                    description: |-
                      Port is the port of the Endpoint Picker extension service.

                      Port is required when the referent is a Kubernetes Service. In this
                      case, the port number is the service port number, not the target port.
                      For other resources, destination port might be derived from the referent
                      resource or this field.
                    properties:
                      number:
                        description: |-
                          Number defines the port number to access the selected model server Pods.
                          The number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
                        format: int32
                        maximum: 65535
                        minimum: 1
                        type: integer
                    required:
                    - number
                    type: object
                required:
                - name
                type: object
                x-kubernetes-validations:
                - message: port is required when kind is 'Service' or unspecified
                    (defaults to 'Service')
                  rule: self.kind != 'Service' || has(self.port)
              selector:
                description: |-
                  Selector determines which Pods are members of this inference pool.
                  It matches Pods by their labels only within the same namespace; cross-namespace
                  selection is not supported.

                  The structure of this LabelSelector is intentionally simple to be compatible
                  with Kubernetes Service selectors, as some implementations may translate
                  this configuration into a Service resource.
                properties:
                  matchLabels:
                    additionalProperties:
                      description: |-
                        LabelValue is the value of a label. This is used for validation
                        of maps. This matches the Kubernetes label validation rules:
                        * must be 63 characters or less (can be empty),
                        * unless empty, must begin and end with an alphanumeric character ([a-z0-9A-Z]),
                        * could contain dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.

                        Valid values include:

                        * MyValue
                        * my.name
                        * 123-my-value
                      maxLength: 63
                      minLength: 0
                      pattern: ^(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?$
                      type: string
                    description: |-
                      MatchLabels contains a set of required {key,value} pairs.
                      An object must match every label in this map to be selected.
                      The matching logic is an AND operation on all entries.
                    maxProperties: 64
                    minProperties: 1
                    type: object
                required:
                - matchLabels
                type: object
              targetPorts:
                description: |-
                  TargetPorts defines a list of ports that are exposed by this InferencePool.
                  Every port will be treated as a distinctive endpoint by EPP,
                  addressable as a 'podIP:portNumber' combination.
                items:
                  description: Port defines the network port that will be exposed
                    by this InferencePool.
                  properties:
                    number:
                      description: |-
                        Number defines the port number to access the selected model server Pods.
                        The number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
                      format: int32
                      maximum: 65535
                      minimum: 1
                      type: integer
                  required:
                  - number
                  type: object
                maxItems: 8
                minItems: 1
                type: array
                x-kubernetes-list-type: atomic
                x-kubernetes-validations:
                - message: port number must be unique
                  rule: self.all(p1, self.exists_one(p2, p1.number==p2.number))
            required:
            - endpointPickerRef
            - selector
            - targetPorts
            type: object
          status:
            description: Status defines the observed state of the InferencePool.
            properties:
              parents:
                description: |-
                  Parents is a list of parent resources, typically Gateways, that are associated with
                  the InferencePool, and the status of the InferencePool with respect to each parent.

                  A controller that manages the InferencePool, must add an entry for each parent it manages
                  and remove the parent entry when the controller no longer considers the InferencePool to
                  be associated with that parent.

                  A maximum of 32 parents will be represented in this list. When the list is empty,
                  it indicates that the InferencePool is not associated with any parents.
                items:
                  description: ParentStatus defines the observed state of InferencePool

                  properties:

                      description: |-

                        state of the InferencePool. This field is required to be set by the controller that
                        manages the InferencePool.

                        Supported condition types are:

                        * "Accepted"
                        * "ResolvedRefs"

                        description: Condition contains details for one aspect of
                          the current state of this API Resource.
                        properties:
                          lastTransitionTime:
                            description: |-
                              lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
                              This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.
                            format: date-time
                            type: string
                          message:
                            description: |-
                              message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
                              This may be an empty string.
                            maxLength: 32768
                            type: string
                          observedGeneration:
                            description: |-
                              observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
                              For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
                              with respect to the current state of the instance.
                            format: int64
                            minimum: 0
                            type: integer
                          reason:
                            description: |-
                              reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
                              Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
                              and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
                              The value should be a CamelCase string.
                              This field may not be empty.
                            maxLength: 1024
                            minLength: 1
                            pattern: ^[A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9_,:]*[A-Za-z0-9_])?$
                            type: string
                          status:
                            description: status of the condition, one of True, False,
                              Unknown.
                            enum:
                            - "True"
                            - "False"
                            - Unknown
                            type: string
                          type:
                            description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.
                            maxLength: 316

                            type: string
                        required:
                        - lastTransitionTime
                        - message

                        - status
                        - type
                        type: object
                      maxItems: 8
                      type: array
                      x-kubernetes-list-map-keys:
                      - type
                      x-kubernetes-list-type: map
                    controllerName:
                      description: |-
                        ControllerName is a domain/path string that indicates the name of the controller that

                        parentRef references a Gateway kind.

                        Example: "example.net/gateway-controller".

                        The format of this field is DOMAIN "/" PATH, where DOMAIN and PATH are valid Kubernetes names:

                         https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

                        Controllers MAY populate this field when writing status. When populating this field, controllers
                        should ensure that entries to status populated with their ControllerName are cleaned up when they
                        are no longer necessary.
                      maxLength: 253
                      minLength: 1
                      pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*\/[A-Za-z0-9\/\-._~%!$&'()*+,;=:]+$

                      description: |-
                        ParentRef is used to identify the parent resource that this status

                      properties:
                        group:
                          default: gateway.networking.k8s.io
                          description: |-
                            Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed
                            to be in the "gateway.networking.k8s.io" API group.
                          maxLength: 253
                          minLength: 0
                          pattern: ^$|^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$
                          type: string
                        kind:
                          default: Gateway
                          description: |-
                            Kind is the kind of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed
                            to be a "Gateway" kind.
                          maxLength: 63
                          minLength: 1
                          pattern: ^[a-zA-Z]([-a-zA-Z0-9]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$
                          type: string
                        name:
                          description: Name is the name of the referent API object.
                          maxLength: 253

                          type: string

                          maxLength: 63

                          pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$
                          type: string
                      required:
                      - name
                      type: object
                  required:
                  - parentRef
                  type: object
                maxItems: 32
                type: array
                x-kubernetes-list-type: atomic
            type: object
